facts.statement: Fossils of Piscogavialis were discovered in 1998 in the Pisco Formation of the Sacaco Basin in southern Peru.
facts.quote: Fossils of Piscogavialis have been found from the Mio-Pliocene Pisco Formation of the Sacaco Basin in southern Peru in 1998

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Piscogavialis is nearly complete and preserved in three dimensions.
facts.quote: The holotype skull is preserved in three dimensions and is nearly complete

facts.statement: A mandible and some postcranial material were found associated with the skull of Piscogavialis.
facts.quote: A mandible and some postcranial material have also been found in association with the skull

facts.statement: Features in the occipital region of the skull support classifying Piscogavialis in the family Gavialidae.
facts.quote: Several important features of the occipital region of the skull support a referral to the family Gavialidae

facts.statement: Strata suggest that Piscogavialis lived in a coastal environment.
facts.quote: The strata from which remains of Piscogavialis have been found suggest that it lived in a coastal environment

facts.statement: During the Miocene, the Pisco Basin in Peru was covered by shallow marine waters connected to the open ocean.
facts.quote: During the Miocene, what is now the Pisco Basin in Peru was largely covered by a shallow marine transgression that connected to the open ocean

facts.statement: The extinction of Peru's marine gavialids, including Piscogavialis, was caused by dropping sea levels, the uplifting of the Andes Mountains, and falling global temperatures during the Pliocene.
facts.quote: Eventually, however, the extinction of Peru's marine gavialids was brought on by the disruption of these coastal ecosystems, caused by dropping sea levels and the uplifting of the Andes Mountains, coupled with the more drastically dropping global temperatures of the Pliocene

facts.statement: A 2007 phylogenetic analysis placed Piscogavialis within the subfamily Gryposuchinae alongside Aktiogavialis, Gryposuchus, Ikanogavialis, and Siquisiquesuchus.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis conducted in a 2007 study found Gryposuchinae to include the genera Aktiogavialis, Gryposuchus, Ikanogavialis, Piscogavialis, and Siquisiquesuchus

facts.statement: A 2018 study suggests that Gryposuchinae, including Piscogavialis, may be paraphyletic and represent an evolutionary grade leading to Gavialis and the gharial.
facts.quote: a 2018 tip dating study by Lee & Yates simultaneously using morphological, molecular (DNA sequencing), and stratigraphic (fossil age) data indicated that the members of Gryposuchinae may in fact be paraphyletic and rather an evolutionary grade towards Gavialis and the gharial

facts.statement: A 2022 study depicts Piscogavialis as a more derived member of the family Gavialidae.
facts.quote: The below cladogram is from the 2022 Salas-Gismondi et al. study describing the newly discovered co-existing Sacacosuchus, and shows Piscogavialis as a more derived member of Gavialidae

facts.statement: The genus Piscogavialis was described by Kraus in 1998.
The fossil range of Piscogavialis spans the Miocene epochs of Huayqueriense and Montehermosense.
Piscogavialis belongs to the family Gavialidae.
Piscogavialis is classified within the subfamily Gryposuchinae.
Piscogavialis is known from only a single specimen.
facts.quote: Piscogavialis es conocido por solo un espécimen

facts.statement: Fossils of Piscogavialis have been found in strata ranging from the Miocene to the Pliocene in the Pisco Formation of the Sacaco Basin in southern Peru.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de Piscogavialis se han encontrado estratos del Mioceno al Plioceno de la Formación Pisco en la Cuenca Sacaco en el sur de Perú

facts.statement: It has been suggested that the strata containing Piscogavialis remains indicate it lived in a coastal environment.
facts.quote: Se ha sugerido que los estratos en que se han encontrado los restos de Piscogavialis indican que vivía en un ambiente costero

facts.statement: However, other gryposuchines have been found in deposits that were clearly freshwater environments.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, se ha hallado también griposuquinos en yacimientos que claramente eran de ambientes de agua dulce
